summary: NAT hairpinning + source-port reuse causing HTTP/2 stream resets during parallel model artifact pulls
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent HTTP/2 stream resets and 502/stream-closed errors when fleet of serving nodes concurrently pull model artifacts over the cluster egress path. Impact: Model pulls fail (partial), causing cold-starts to time out and downstream inference requests to error or stall. Environment: Private deployment behind customer TGW and a pair of NAT gateways in us-east-1; TLS termination at Redwood control-plane; model artifacts served from S3 via VPC endpoint and from a hosted artifact proxy (HTTPS) over egress.
impact: Multiple serving hosts experience simultaneous aborted model downloads during rollout/scale events. Symptoms include ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_CANCEL, repeated TLS rehandshakes, elevated retry rates in serving runtime, and increased inference latency leading to user errors in production.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a scale-up event for a model (llama-3-8b) to 50 replicas in the customer's private cluster.
2) Trigger parallel artifact downloads by restarting pods to force cold pulls.
3) Monitor egress NAT gateway connection table and serving runtime logs.
4) Observe duplicated source-port allocations and TCP connection resets between serving hosts and artifact proxy/S3 endpoint.
observed_behavior: Concurrent downloads frequently fail with http2 stream resets; server logs show repeated TCP FIN/RST from remote and client-side 'stream cancelled' errors. Packet captures indicate multiple distinct internal IPs mapping to a small set of external source ports due to hairpinning/masquerade behavior, leading to collisions and stream demux failures in the artifact proxy or intermediate stateful device.
expected_behavior: Each internal connection should be NATed to a unique (ip,port) tuple so concurrent HTTP/2 streams don't collide when translated across the egress path. No stream-level resets during parallel artifact pulls.
logs: tcpdump excerpt: client 10.0.5.23:51432 -> proxy 54.239.0.12:443, then client 10.0.6.11:51432 -> proxy 54.239.0.12:443 with same src port observed within 10ms
Artifact proxy logs: 'http2: stream id 19 cancelled by peer (duplicate client port detected)'
Serving runtime: 'model-pull: permanent failure after 3 retries, error=http2: stream canceled'
comments: 2026-03-10 09:02 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported ~15% of cold starts failed during a scale event. Provided initial logs and pcap. Asked customer to temporarily stagger restarts as a mitigation.

2026-03-10 09:47 - Jonas Meyer (SRE): Observed source-port reuse in NAT conntrack snapshot. Hypothesis: TGW/NAT hairpinning + asymmetric SNAT policy is causing multiple internal IPs to be mapped to identical external 5-tuple when hairpin path uses different ENIs.
2026-03-10 12:30 - Customer (NovaCommerce): Confirmed they recently added a second NAT gateway in a different AZ and enabled route propagation through TGW. Issues started ~1 hour after change.
2026-03-11 08:15 - Jonas Meyer (SRE): Reproduced in staging by creating two subnets and forcing NAT hairpin with source port overlap. Filed infra PR to change SNAT algorithm (see linked PR).
investigation_notes: Conntrack entries show SNAT collisions where the external 5-tuple is identical for different internal IPs: this causes stateful middleboxes/artifact proxy to misassociate streams.
Artifact proxy implements per-(ip,port) demultiplexing for HTTP/2 streams and treats colliding src ports as duplicate sessions; upstream then cancels existing streams.
Issue is exacerbated when customer introduces multiple NAT gateways/ENIs and TGW routes create hairpin return paths where egressing interface differs from ingress.

Related prior ticket SUP-27654 documents ephemeral nat-port reuse patterns; this case differs because hairpinning changes which NAT device performs translation leading to identical port reuse across devices.
Packet-level timing shows collisions occur within <50ms during a burst of simultaneous connections, explaining why high-concurrency cold starts are affected.
Tested mitigation: enabling ephemeral port randomization and increasing source port range on customer NAT reduced collision rate in staging.
workaround_and_mitigation: Short-term: Customer to stagger restarts by 5s per replica to reduce parallelism of model pulls.
Short-term: Increase NAT ephemeral port range on customer side (recommended 32768-65535) and enable source-port randomization where supported.
Medium-term: Route artifact pulls through single egress NAT path (disable hairpinning across TGW for artifact proxy origin) to ensure consistent SNAT device and port assignment.
Long-term: We will add a note in the Private Deploy runbook advising customers to avoid multi-NAT hairpinning patterns for large-scale parallel artifact pulls and provide recommended NAT settings.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Implemented customer change: set NAT ephemeral port range to 32768-61000 and configured TGW to prefer single egress attachment for artifact-origin routes. Observed zero stream-reset failures in subsequent scale test (100 concurrent pulls).
2026-03-12 - Infra PR merged to add guardrails in our on-agent egress configuration that detect high port-reuse rates and log a warning to Console (github PR #812).
Follow-up: Create a KB article explaining the NAT hairpinning failure mode and recommended network settings for private deployments (owner: Jonas Meyer, due 2026-03-20).
